$description: BDL terminology glossary: the authority for how product terms are rendered in each supported locale. English is canonical. `translatable: false` marks a term that is BDL syntax, notation or a protocol identity and is never rendered in another language. Edited by hand; checked by scripts/check_l10n.py.

terms.context: A named value the product senses, decides or shows; a node on the canvas. The BDL keyword `concept` is never translated.
terms.note: Keep as a noun; do not render as 'idea'.

terms.context: A relationship between concepts as the kernel and the protocol name it (`mapping` keyword, MappingId).
terms.note: Studio's prose says 'relationship' for the same thing; keep the two consistent within one locale.

terms.context: Studio's product word for a mapping: how one concept follows from others.

A relationship without inputs and without a definition at the environment boundary: a value entering the behavior model from the environment, observed once per activation (ADR-0032). The canvas header word, the inspector's Role, the library section (plural: Sources) and the Simulate page's section.
terms.note: Never 'sensor', never 'signal', never a file, never source code. In ja avoid ソース, which reads as source code; in zh-Hans avoid 源代码/信号源/传感器.

terms.context: The Standard Library: ready-made items — a Concept item (one concept) or a Source item (a concept and the Source that provides it) — that instantiate ordinary objects (docs/spec/concept-library.md). The sidebar tab and the Studio section words Concepts / Sources.
terms.note: An item is a way of making objects, never an identity; say 'item', never 'template', in new text.

terms.context: What is outside the behavior model and provides a Source's value ('provided by the environment'). Distinct from the library group 'environment' (temperature, light, …), which is about what is measured.
What a relationship is where the designer is: Source, Relationship, or the port it backs (requires / provides / parameter). Derived, never stored.
A `.bdl` file of the project, in the Code view.
terms.note: Distinct from the Source role; always say 'file' in the translation.

terms.context: The `output` declaration: where a value leaves the design; the keyword is never translated.
An output of a component that is private, one per instance.
The value form of a concept: quantity, on/off, count, collection, grouped, optional.
terms.note: Studio's short form is 'value form' (值形式 / 値の形式).

terms.context: How an interface is backed: the definitions and devices that make a promise good.
terms.note: Not 'implementation' in the software sense when the subject is a promise.

terms.context: A group of relationships seen together; a way of seeing, never a change of meaning.
A reusable behavior with a promise (ports) and its own source.
A component's ports as instances see them.
A value committed to an output at an activation; also the component's promise.
terms.note: 'commit' as a verb: 提交 / コミット.

terms.context: The kernel's name for a timing domain (`clock` in the protocol).
When a group of relationships and outputs update together; a name, not a rate.
Placing a design's outputs on a board's devices.
The board a deployment is checked against; also 'final target' for the output an instance's value reaches.
terms.note: 'final target' → 最终目标 / 最終ターゲット.

terms.context: The formula attached to a mapping.
The expression text of a definition.
Stepping the design tick by tick with chosen inputs.
Live values from a running target (roadmap).
The relationship that commits a value to an output.
A link from a provided or top-level value into a required port; converts nothing.
What a device asks of the board (a pin, a peripheral).
terms.note: 'requires' as a port kind stays the English keyword.

terms.context: What a board offers to requirements.
A measurement unit of a quantity.
terms.note: Unit symbols (m, s, °C) are never translated.

terms.context: Same as Unit, in prose.
The type `()` of a mapping with no inputs. Prose may name it; the notation `()` is always shown as is.
The role of a port or mapping that brings a value in from the environment.
The kernel's normalised type of a mapping (`() -> B` is `B`).
A placed component.
A declared point of a component's promise.
One diagnostic as the Inspector lists it.
A one-click edit the daemon proposes for a finding.

The empty product type as written.
The stable identity of a diagnostic.
terms.note: Identity; localized presentation lives beside it, never instead of it.
